root.name: Nimzo-Indian Defense: Mikenas Attack
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. Qd3

overview: White plays 4.Qd3, an old line that guards c4 and the knight on c3 without allowing the doubled pawns of 4.Qc2 lines. Black usually replies 4...c5 or 4...d5 or 4...Nc6, challenging the centre at once. The queen on d3 is slightly awkward, so White gets a solid but modest edge at best.

white_ideas.idea: Keep the c3 knight protected without doubled pawns
Develop with a3 or e4 as needed
Use the queen on the d3-f5 diagonal

black_ideas.idea: Pin the knight with ...Bb4 and exchange on c3 if useful

typical_structures.structure: Nimzo-Indian centre with d4 and c4 pawns against Black's pin

character.notes: Both sides play the usual Nimzo plans without forced lines.

structure.notes: The d4/c4 centre is under pressure and not yet fixed.

approach.notes: Rarely played by strong players against the Nimzo.

level.notes: Not a lot of theory but still Nimzo structures.

character.reason: Neither forcing nor especially hard to break down.

gambit.reason: There is no gambit at the root.

soundness.reason: Qd3 is an unambitious but accepted way to avoid doubled pawns.

structure.reason: The centre stays in tension while Black chooses between ...c5 and ...d5.

approach.reason: Seldom chosen by strong players against the Nimzo.

level.reason: Nimzo ideas need understanding but not a heavy load of theory.

plans.reason: Black can give up the bishop for the knight or White can try to keep the bishop pair.
